sections.title: Reading depth switch test
sections.what: Checks that switching between Quick, Tactical and Analyst changes the text of the first Desk item as expected and that the Analyst choice survives a reload.
sections.why: Makes sure the detail choice is both working and remembered, which users notice directly.
sections.watch_out: Assertions match exact wording, so the test is sensitive to copy edits.

summary: Browser test of the Desk's three reading depths, Quick, Tactical and Analyst, checking the text changes, stays sourced, and is remembered after reload.
purpose: Confirms users can choose how much detail they see, and that the choice sticks.
why: Different users want different levels of detail, so the depth choice must work and persist.
how: It opens the Desk, reads the first item in Quick mode and expects one line. It then selects Tactical and expects a sentence about win chances changing across six balls, then Analyst and expects the method line. After a reload, it expects Analyst to still be selected.
inputs: The Desk page and its first item, which depends on the seeded data.
outputs: Pass or fail for each depth and the saved choice.
risks: The expected sentences are specific, so any change in the wording or data will fail the test.
debug: Compare the text on the page with the expected pattern. If the saved choice is lost, check how the depth setting is stored.
